description: ol-reserved-word (issue #837, maintainer ruling #833): binding a keyword is FREE in every form. spec/grammar.md:386 states it as a normative MUST: every binding form "MUST accept **any** name, including a keyword, a primitive, or an alias spelling of one ... An implementation MUST NOT raise `ol-reserved-word` -- or any other diagnostic -- for the name alone in any of those positions, at any stage." The bindings here each put a keyword (spec/grammar.md:368-376) in a different form -- assignment's colon-place `:repeat = 1` and bare-place `set while to 2`, a `for ... in` binder, a `map` binder, a `reduce` accumulator, one name of a destructuring pattern, and a required procedure parameter -- and every one is accepted. Enforcement sits at the four declaration slots instead, which spec/grammar.md:388 explains is what makes the rule unbypassable: "A restriction on a binding form is bypassable, because `local` is optional and the same name can be bound with `<place> = <value>` instead; the four declaration slots are the only way to register a callable, so there is nothing to bypass." reserved-word-define-reserved pins the other half. `"check": true` (semantic-checker only) because this is a checker rule -- nothing is executed and no events are produced.
